title: Dune - Host, VM and services
description: R740 host clocks, temperatures and NUMA, dune-prod guest load, and supporting services (meta#99).

panels.title: Host core clock, average
panels.description: Average of all 80 host CPUs.

panels.title: Host core clock, fastest
panels.description: Fastest host CPU. Turbo limit is 3.9 GHz.

panels.title: Host hottest sensor
panels.description: Hottest host temperature sensor.

panels.title: Guest memory used
panels.description: Share of dune-prod memory in use.

panels.title: Guest vCPU busy, average
panels.description: Average busy share across dune-prod's 60 vCPUs.

panels.title: Prometheus series
panels.description: Active series in dune-prod's Prometheus.

panels.title: Host core clock
panels.description: Average, fastest and slowest host CPU. After the BIOS change busy cores should reach about 3.8-3.9 GHz (earlier they peaked near 3.2-3.3 GHz).

panels.title: Host temperatures
panels.description: Hottest and average host temperature sensor.

panels.title: Host NUMA misses per second
panels.description: Memory pages placed on a remote node (numa_miss), skipped (numa_foreign) or allocated for another node (numa_other). Remote access is about 2x slower.

panels.title: Guest vCPU busy
panels.description: Average and busiest vCPU of dune-prod over a 15 s window.

panels.title: Service CPU (cores)
panels.description: Director, RabbitMQ (beam.smp), Postgres, Docker and monitoring, from process-exporter.

panels.title: Guest memory
panels.description: Used share of dune-prod memory.

panels.title: VM CPU use (share of each VM's vCPUs)
panels.description: From the Proxmox API (read-only token), per VM. 1.0 means every vCPU of that VM is fully busy.

panels.title: VM memory used (share of each VM's RAM)
panels.description: From the Proxmox API, per VM, as seen by the hypervisor.

panels.title: Board temperatures (IPMI)
panels.description: CPU packages, air inlet (case intake) and exhaust, from the board's sensors via in-band IPMI (15 s).

panels.title: Fan speed (IPMI)
panels.description: Six chassis fans. A fan dropping or stopping shows here before temperatures rise.

panels.title: Server power draw (IPMI)
panels.description: Whole-server power in watts (DCMI).

panels.title: Network errors and drops
panels.description: Packets the NIC reported as errored or dropped, per second: guest eth0 and host nic0, in and out. Should sit at zero; steady non-zero values point at a cable, switch port, driver or full queue.

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: Share of outgoing TCP segments that had to be sent again (5 min). Rises with packet loss or a congested path; a few tenths of a percent is normal.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time the system disk had I/O in flight (5 min): guest sda and host sda. Near 100% means the disk is the limit.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: Average time per completed read and write (5 min). Gaps mean no I/O in the window. Sustained tens of milliseconds is a slow disk.

panels.title: Disk I/O pressure
panels.description: Share of time tasks were waiting on disk I/O (Linux pressure stall, 1 min). Zero is healthy.

panels.title: Host storage used
panels.description: Share used of the Proxmox thin pool that holds the VM disks (local-lvm) and of the host's root storage (local). A full thin pool freezes every VM on it.

panels.title: Swap activity
panels.description: Memory moved to and from swap, bytes per second (5 min). In is a page read back from swap, out is a page written. Should be zero; sustained activity means memory pressure.
